title: Multiplication of Vectors — Vector (Cross) Product
notes: **Definition**: if $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are two vectors inclined at angle $\theta$, their vector product (cross product) is $\vec{A}\times\vec{B}=AB\sin\theta\,\hat{n}$, where $\hat{n}$ is a unit vector perpendicular to the plane containing $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$, with direction given by the right-hand rule. The result is a vector: $\vec{C}=\vec{A}\times\vec{B}$.
**Case 1 — parallel vectors**: if $\theta=0°$, $\vec{A}\times\vec{B}=0$. This is the condition for two vectors to be parallel.
**Case 2 — perpendicular vectors**: if $\theta=90°$, $|\vec{A}\times\vec{B}|=AB$ (maximum). This is the condition for two vectors to be perpendicular.

**Non-commutative property**: $\vec{A}\times\vec{B} = -(\vec{B}\times\vec{A})$, i.e. reversing the order reverses the direction of the resultant vector (cross product does NOT commute, unlike the dot product).

**Cross products of unit vectors**: $\hat{i}\times\hat{i}=\hat{j}\times\hat{j}=\hat{k}\times\hat{k}=0$ (parallel to themselves). For the mutually perpendicular set (right-hand rule, cyclic order $i\to j\to k\to i$): $\hat{i}\times\hat{j}=\hat{k}$, $\hat{j}\times\hat{k}=\hat{i}$, $\hat{k}\times\hat{i}=\hat{j}$; and reversing order flips sign: $\hat{j}\times\hat{i}=-\hat{k}$, $\hat{k}\times\hat{j}=-\hat{i}$, $\hat{i}\times\hat{k}=-\hat{j}$.
